skill.displayName: 标前分析助手-投标前必查的一份报告

llm.summary: The skill performs the advertised bid analysis, but it also persists credentials, collects a hashed device identifier for auto-registration, and preserves login-bypass signed links in shareable reports.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to the vendor API fit the purpose, but sending a stable MAC-derived hash for account creation and embedding access-bearing URLs in local outputs are higher-risk than necessary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The metadata declares only ZLBX_API_KEY, while the artifacts also describe reading local bid files, writing reports, and storing credentials under ~/.zlbx/config.json.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registration is consent-gated and cost limits are disclosed, but default HTML export and preserving sk signed URLs lack sufficient user warning for sharing risk.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes API keys to a home-directory config file and generates shareable HTML reports by default, including full absolute paths and signed links.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The bid-analysis workflow is coherent, but account auto-registration, device-derived identifiers, recharge/login handling, and signed link propagation expand the capability beyond analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review carefully before installing. Use a manually created API key if possible, avoid auto-registration if you do not want device-derived identifiers sent, and do not share generated HTML reports unless you are comfortable exposing signed detail-page links and local report contents.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local file reading and report writing are disclosed and relevant to analyzing user-provided bid materials, but they are underdeclared in metadata.
[TP4] expected: HTML report generation is explicitly part of the report workflow and the renderer escapes dynamic text, but the default shareable artifact increases exposure.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Auto-registration and account lifecycle handling support onboarding, not bid analysis itself; consent is required, so this is a Review concern rather than malicious behavior.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The artifact explicitly collects platform, architecture, and a SHA-256 MAC-derived hash for trial deduplication; this stable device signal is not necessary for analysis.
[SDI-2] expected: API key use is required for the vendor service, but persisting the key in ~/.zlbx/config.json creates long-lived local credential handling outside the declared env requirement.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Recharge, auto-login SID generation, and phone-binding guidance are account-management behavior rather than procurement analysis.
[SSD-3] unexpected: The artifacts explicitly require retaining sk parameters described as login-bypass signatures in chat and HTML/JSON outputs, creating a credible token-sharing risk.
[E1] unexpected: External POSTs for bid data are expected, but transmitting device-linked registration features is outside the core analysis workflow even though it is disclosed and consent-gated.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese instructions match the artifact language and target workflow; this is more of a usability risk than a security driver for the verdict.
